records.text: CBS filled the audience with college Republicans and questions selected by CBS for Erika Kirk's town hall
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: They filled the audience with people selected by CBS, college Republicans, with questions selected by CBS.

verification.notes: CBS confirms the town hall used an invited audience, and the attendee form reported by the Guardian confirms CBS recruited attendees for a prerecorded event. CBS described the group more broadly around faith, political violence, and the political right. I found no public attendee list establishing that the audience was filled specifically with College Republicans, nor a public production record proving every question was selected by CBS. The controlled invited-audience portion is confirmed; the narrower composition and question-selection claims remain unconfirmed.

records.text: Is the United States "hot" because officials lied about six servicemen who died until the truth leaked to CBS News?
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: President Donald J. Trump. Was that written by Mark Levin? Like when he was six or who put this message together, the hottest country in the world, because we're bombing kids for no reason because we just killed 150 schoolgirls for no reason because you guys just lied about six of our servicemen who died and they had to leak that to CBS News that you were lying about what was happening. Is that what makes us hot?

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. CBS interviewed Army survivors of the Kuwait drone attack that killed six service members; they directly disputed the Pentagon description of a fortified position and said their unit lacked defenses and was unprepared. This supports that the official account was materially challenged by participants, but available evidence does not prove officials knowingly lied or that the later account was a leak rather than survivor reporting.

records.text: Bari Weiss founded and held an ownership stake in The Free Press before becoming editor-in-chief of CBS News.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Before we get to what he had to say about Bari Weiss, I want to remind you that Bari Weiss started and is a part-owner, at least, of The Free Press before that—before she went on to CBS News.

verification.notes: The legacy false result reversed the meaning of the transcript. Owens said Weiss founded and held a stake in The Free Press before going on to CBS News. The Free Press identifies Weiss as its founder; CBS and AP report that Paramount acquired the outlet founded in 2021 and, as part of that October 2025 transaction, Weiss moved from co-founder/CEO to editor-in-chief of CBS News. The sequence asserted in the episode is therefore true. The erroneous legacy determination remains preserved in legacy_claim_provenance.
